rating.reasoning_summary: This strand centers on a single viral insight—'your dad was just some guy'—and explores its recursive application: if authority figures are 'just people,' then so are you, and so is everyone else. The discourse moves through three phases: (1) Initial catharsis of de-pedestaling parents (2021-2022), (2) Analytical expansion into trauma/resentment dynamics and role-based vs. cosmic blame (2022), and (3) Philosophical maturation into elderhood/sovereignty themes (2024-2025). The boundary object is the original tweet itself, which becomes a touchstone for discussions of hierarchy, projection, and psychological development. This is primarily *constructive* rather than dialectical—people build on the frame rather than challenging it—but it demonstrates high *semantic evolution* as the concept gets applied to Jesus, friends, political leaders, and self-perception. The strand's weakness is its *diffuseness*: after 2022, references become sporadic and lack the tight causal linkage of earlier threads. Still, it produces durable vocabulary ('hierarchy-cucked,' 'just some guy') and connects personal psychology to systems critique.

essential_tweets.annotation: The Artifact: The original viral tweet establishing the core frame
First Refinement: Shifting from 'deflation' to 'empathy'—dad as protagonist of his own story
The Role Frame: Introducing 'bad parent ≠ bad person' (job-based accountability)
Trauma Dynamics: Visa identifying cosmic injustice vs. food poisoning as competing frames for harm
Generalization as Defense: Why people prefer 'all X are bad' over 'I was personally targeted'
Theological Expansion: Applying 'just some guy' to Buddha and Jesus
The Recursive Turn: 'You're just a guy, but so was everyone who achieved great things'
Peer Trauma: Visa applying the frame to childhood friends ('just a bunch of kids')
Canonization: Visa declaring this Rival's best tweet, cementing its status as boundary object
Political Synthesis: Linking psychological immaturity to 'picking a king' in democracy
